Detailed method

The calculator opens at 400 g flour, 65% hydration, 1.8% salt, and 0.8% yeast. The balls fields open at 4 pieces of about 168 g, four skillet breads from this batch. Cook them on a hot dry pan until they blister. Butter, garlic, or herbs after cooking are optional and are not in the gram total. The photo shows breads brushed that way. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Mix Stir 400 g flour, 260 g water, 7.2 g salt, and 3.2 g instant yeast, then knead about 6 minutes until smooth and soft. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  2. Rise Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for 60 to 90 minutes, until it has about doubled.
  3. Divide Cut 4 pieces of about 168 g, the weight in the balls fields. Cover and rest 15 minutes.
  4. Roll Dust the counter lightly. Roll each piece into an oval about 20 cm long and about 6 mm thick. Do not roll them paper thin or they will not blister.
  5. Cook Heat a dry skillet until a drop of water skitters. Cook one bread at a time, about 60 to 90 seconds on the first side, until bubbles jump up. Flip it and cook about 45 to 60 seconds, until both sides have dark spots. No oil in the pan.
  6. Brush Stack them in a cloth so they stay flexible. A brush of butter, garlic, or herbs goes on after cooking and is extra.
  7. Serve Eat them while they are still soft. A dry skillet reheats one that has firmed up.
